pages.section: Writing workshop / Writing task / Understand the task

writing_task.title: A for and against essay
writing_task.instructions: Write an essay discussing the advantages and disadvantages of different kinds of technology. Your essay should end with your own opinion, and state if you are for or against using this kind of technology.

exercises.prompt: Study the writing task. What do you have to do in the essay?
exercises.answer_key: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of a chosen technology, end with a personal opinion, and state whether you are for or against using that kind of technology.

exercises.prompt: Read the model essay and answer the questions.

questions.question: Which topic is the essay about?
Is the writer for or against the topic? Why?
questions.answer_key: Against. The writer prefers downloading because they believe it is much better to own the music you love.

exercises.prompt: Answer the questions about the model essay.

questions.question: How does the writer begin paragraphs 2 and 3?
questions.answer_key: Paragraph 2 begins with: 'Let's start with the advantages.' Paragraph 3 begins with: 'Turning to the disadvantages,...'

questions.question: How many advantages are described in paragraph 2?
questions.answer_key: 4 advantages (listen anywhere on any device without using memory; create and share playlists / get recommendations; choice is enormous; possible to stream for free).

questions.question: How many disadvantages are described in paragraph 3?
questions.answer_key: 4 disadvantages (need good Wi-Fi and data allowance / service can be expensive or free service has annoying ads; audio quality can be poor; some artists don't appear / aren't paid much; you don't own the music).

questions.question: Which points does the conclusion contain: advantages, disadvantages, new information, opinion?
questions.answer_key: Advantages ('convenience of streaming') and opinion ('it's much better to own the music you love', 'I still prefer downloads').

model_essay.title: IS IT TIME TO STOP DOWNLOADING?
model_essay.paragraph_1_introduction: How do you listen to music? Increasingly, the big question is whether to forget downloads and just listen to music on streaming services, which now account for 75% of the music industry's income. So what are the advantages and disadvantages of doing this?
model_essay.paragraph_2_advantages: Let's start with the advantages. First, and most importantly, streaming means you can listen to your favorite songs anywhere, on any device, without using up memory on it. Second, you can create your own playlists, and what's more, share them with friends easily. Another big advantage is that streaming services suggest music to you, which helps you find new bands. On top of this, the choice is absolutely enormous! Finally, it's possible to stream music for free, which is great for young people.
model_essay.paragraph_3_disadvantages: Turning to the disadvantages, first of all you need good Wi-Fi for streaming and a fairly big data allowance. As well as the cost of these, the streaming service itself can be pretty expensive (and while the free service with ads might seem fine at first, obviously they can get very annoying). Furthermore, the audio quality can be quite poor, although not everyone notices this. There's also the fact that some artists don't appear on streaming services, and another argument against them is that they don't pay artists much. Last but not least, when you stream music, unfortunately you don't own it at all.
model_essay.paragraph_4_conclusion: So, all things considered, even though I like the convenience of streaming, to me personally, it's much better to own the music you love. That's why overall, I still prefer downloads.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing tip
tips_and_strategies.content:
Don't decide which topic you are going to write about too quickly. First, ask yourself:
• Which of the technology topics are you most familiar with?
• Which have you heard people talk about the most?
• Which one(s) do you use most often?
• Which one(s) have you had the most problems with?

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing strategy: Organizing for and against points
tips_and_strategies.content: In a for and against essay, it's easiest to discuss the advantages in one paragraph, and then do the same for the disadvantages in another paragraph.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing tip
tips_and_strategies.content: Before you begin writing, make notes on the essay topic. You can write down nouns or adjectives under "for" or "against." This will help you organize your ideas and save time. After taking notes, try cutting as many words as possible from your ideas, leaving only the key information you need. This will help you get into the habit of taking short notes.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing strategy: Generating ideas
tips_and_strategies.content:
Before you decide whether you are for or against the topic, think of as many points as possible for each argument. Think of different people you know and their opinions.
You can find more ideas by doing online research and choosing the ideas that you think are strongest.

exercises.prompt: Study the writing tip and discuss your ideas with a partner.
Study the writing strategy. Match these notes to the different essay topics. Which notes are about advantages? Which are about disadvantages?

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing strategy: Selecting and ordering ideas
tips_and_strategies.content:
There won't be space for more than two or three ideas in each main paragraph. Which ones in your notes make the strongest arguments? Which will be easiest for you to explain?
Decide the order of your ideas now. Which come after each other most logically? Could any of them be joined into one sentence? You can also decide whether to start each paragraph with the strongest points, or finish it with them.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing tip
tips_and_strategies.content: Use the first paragraph to introduce the topic and get the reader's interest. You can make it personal by asking a question. You could also say why it's important to think about this topic, and what the alternative is to using this kind of technology.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing strategy: Linking your for and against ideas
tips_and_strategies.content: In each of the main paragraphs, you need to use words and phrases that link your ideas together and help the reader to understand your arguments. You can use words and expressions for listing and adding ideas.

exercises.prompt: Study the writing strategy (Organizing for and against points) on page 133. Write down your arguments in the For or Against column, and then write what another person might say in answer to them. Do some internet research to find other ideas.
Work in pairs. Read one column of your arguments to each other. The other person has to make an opposite argument for each point. Did you find any new ideas?
Study the writing strategy and answer the questions.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing tip
tips_and_strategies.content: When you talk about the disadvantages, you can make a short contrast with an advantage. Use the key phrases.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing strategy: Using attitude adverbs
tips_and_strategies.content: Attitude adverbs (Obviously, Certainly, Most importantly) are an easy way to make a point clear, as they are only one or two words. They also make your writing more interesting.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing strategy: Introducing for and against paragraphs
tips_and_strategies.content: To make it clear what each of your main paragraphs are about, introduce it with one of these expressions.

introducing_the_advantages: Let's start by looking at the advantages.
introducing_the_disadvantages: Now let's look at some of the disadvantages of ....

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing strategy: Writing a conclusion
tips_and_strategies.content: Your conclusion should be a short final paragraph that repeats one or two of the most important points to you and concludes with a clear statement of your opinion.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing tip
tips_and_strategies.content: Your conclusion should sum up the whole argument, so it helps to include one of the opposite points of view before you give your own opinion. Use one of the key phrases for making a contrast (although, even if, even though, while). Which opposite point of view is mentioned in the conclusion of the model essay?

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing tip (Review and edit)
tips_and_strategies.content:
Avoid repetition when you refer back to something you said earlier, e.g.,
You can play your songs on any device, without using up memory on the device.
You can do this by using pronouns such as:
it  this  that  these  those  them  which
E.g., You can play your songs on any device, without using up memory on it.

exercises.prompt:
Study the writing strategy and look at the key phrases. Now write a draft of your two main paragraphs, using your notes. Remember to include some attitude adverbs and some key phrases for:
• introducing each paragraph
• listing and adding points
• making a contrast
Study the writing strategy about writing an essay conclusion. Which key phrases are used in the model essay on page 132?
Study the key phrases and the writing tip. Then write a draft of your conclusion.

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing tip
tips_and_strategies.content:
Use adverbs of degree with adjectives to make your writing more interesting.
a little -> quite -> fairly -> pretty -> very -> extremely -> incredibly

tips_and_strategies.title: Final check / Writing strategy: Making cuts
tips_and_strategies.content:
If your essay is too long, look for things you can cut without losing any important arguments. If you can't cut things, can you find ways to say the same thing in fewer words?
If necessary, take a break and then try to make more cuts. You can often see new ways to make cuts after a break!

tips_and_strategies.title: Writing tip
tips_and_strategies.content: Read your essay aloud as a final check. Do all the arguments in it make sense? Reading aloud can also help you to see if some information is missing.
